x: In the field events we had Miska 3rd in the Weight, Whitehead 3rd in the Javelin, Luxon 3rd in the Long Jump, and our only win was by our Nigerian high jumper E.

In the Senior events we saw Holtum win the 100 yards, and he was also 2nd in the 220, while Bill Lucas won the 1 mile in 4 min. 36.3 secs., and John Bromley, making a return after an operation for appendicitis, was 2nd to Peter Pirie in the 2 miles. E.
Don Maclean turned out for us in the 2 miles run and did well to finish 4th, and we cannot make out what happens to our distance men for these evening matches. E.
However, we do appear to have three very promising youngsters in this event, and may have a "Savidge" in our midst! Jim Purdy retained his junior High Jump title with a leap of 5 feet, and E.

The 1 mile also saw only one Belgrave representative in Ray Tooby, but here again he was more than a match for the opposition, and Ray won in the good time of 4 min. 21 secs. In the field events we had E.
We also did well in the field events and Jack Chappell was very pleased with the good response to his “ cards ” and is already looking forward to great things from his section next season. E.
Luxon was 2nd in the Triple Jump with a leap of 42ft. 6½ins. E.
All the events are in relay form, with the field events being taken on the aggregate of two members from each club. In the High Jump we had E.

Basil Walden, who was the holder of the 100 yds. title, got into the 2nd round of this event, but could not progress further, and he does not seem to be running with the same dash as he displayed last season. E.
Held at the White City on July 10th-11th, and on the Friday we saw the heats of the 100 yards, and we had Holtum, Mayers and Walden competing, but without success. E.
Maddicks third, and the latter is actually a junior but seems to do better with the senior implement. E.
The Wandsworth Council promoted a 14 miles road run in connection with their Coronation celebrations, and Geoff Pearson finished 3rd, with Len Rolls 8th and Bert Smith 15th. E.
